title: Entry Word Followed by Lowercase Definition

illustrates.quote: d. Leave two blank cells between the entry-word segment and the definition segment when it is not followed by punctuation, capitalization, or enclosure symbols.

items.def: a word formed by using the initial letters of other words: radar (*ra*dio *d*etecting *a*nd *r*anging)

print.printFeatures: Bold entry word; inside the parentheses only the initial letters are italic: ra of radio, d of detecting, a of and, r of ranging; the parentheses and "radar" are roman.

braille.notes: Lines start at cell 1, with runovers at cell 3 (1-3 dictionary format). Two blank spaces separate the entry word 'acronym' from the definition.

printCorrections.was: radar “*radio* *detecting* *and* *ranging*” (curly quotes, four whole italic words)
printCorrections.now: radar (*ra*dio *d*etecting *a*nd *r*anging) (plain parentheses, italic initial letters only)
printCorrections.evidence: references/bana/braille-formats-2016.pdf p.566, rendered at 300 dpi and cropped to the Example 21-18 box: "words: radar (radio detecting and ranging)" with italic only on "ra", "d", "a" and "r" - the first letters spelling radar; no quotation marks. The gold braille (.1ra.'dio .2detect+ .2& .2rang+) is therefore not garbled: it is per-letter italics, as the print shows.

printCorrections.was: Bold entry word; bold word within the definition; italicized phrase within parentheses in the definition.
printCorrections.now: Bold entry word; only the initial letters (ra, d, a, r) inside the parentheses are italic; "radar" is not bold
printCorrections.evidence: references/bana/braille-formats-2016.pdf p.566 (same crop): "radar" is roman, not bold.
